newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium faces second day of rail strike mayhem.
newsitem.headline: Belgium faces second day of rail strike mayhem.

text.p: Belgium faces a day of travel chaos on Tuesday with rail workers set to hold a second 24-hour strike over reorganisation plans that could also hit the Brussels to London Eurostar service.
The selective strike, which follows one a week ago, was set to begin at 10 p.m. (2000 GMT) on Monday night.

Most affected regions are likely to be the south west and north east of the country, but Belgian railways also warned on Monday that the high-speed Paris-Brussels-Amsterdam service could be disrupted as well as the Eurostar.
It advised travellers to head for the northern French city of Lille to board services to London, Paris and the south of France.
Rail unions fear that the rail restructuring plans are in preparation for privatisation and that their jobs could be at risk.
A third 24-hour strike targetting the Brussels region is pencilled in for Friday, although it is not certain it will take place with rail unions and management due to meet on Tuesday.
